extracted.intended_audience: Executive Council, Trainers Leadership Group, Trainers, and the broader Carpentries community
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation/report of The Carpentries Instructor Training program describing the program goals, measurement instruments, outcome metrics (skills, knowledge, motivation, perceptions), certification/checkout metrics, demographic and growth statistics, and actionable recommendations for program improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructor Training program goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduce trainees to evidence-based best practices of teaching; teach how to create a positive environment for learners at The Carpentries workshops; provide opportunities for trainees to practice and build their teaching skills; help trainees become integrated into The Carpentries community; prepare trainees to use these teaching skills in teaching The Carpentries workshops.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These stated goals form the basis for assessing whether the Instructor Training meets its mission; outcomes (skills, knowledge, motivation, perceptions) are measured relative to these goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data sources for assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Two primary sources of data: pre- and post-Instructor Training surveys, and programmatic data from The Carpentries AMY database.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surveys capture trainee perceptions of skills, knowledge, motivation, and trainer performance; AMY database provides counts and historical programmatic information (number/locations of trainings, trainee numbers, certification rates, trainer counts, teaching activity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to teach using live coding
rubrics_metrics.description: Trainees rate their ability to teach using live coding on a five-point Likert scale from 'Extremely able' to 'Not at all able'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to detect pre/post shifts; report notes larger increases here because live coding is covered and practiced during Instructor Training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to create a Carpentries workshop website
rubrics_metrics.description: Trainees rate their ability to create a Carpentries workshop website on the same five-point scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported as an area with smaller gains; many Trainers tend to skip this exercise, indicating a curriculum/process gap to address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to use a concept map for lesson planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Trainees rate their ability to use a concept map for lesson planning on the five-point scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although covered extensively in training, trainees show mixed gains and some struggle with this topic—flag for curriculum strengthening.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to write multiple choice questions with diagnostic power
rubrics_metrics.description: Trainees rate their ability to write diagnostic multiple choice questions on a five-point scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre/post comparisons indicate movement toward greater ability; used as an indicator of assessment-writing skill taught in training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to write effective learning objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Trainees rate their ability to write effective learning objectives on a five-point scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre/post increases observed; used to evaluate trainees' ability to articulate intended outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge of formative vs. summative assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Trainees rate knowledge on a three-point scale from 'Extensive knowledge' to 'Little or no knowledge' about formative vs. summative assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to detect knowledge gains; pre/post shifts from 'little to no' toward 'some' or 'extensive' are considered success indicators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge of giving effective feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Trainees rate their knowledge of how to give effective feedback on the three-point scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observed increases from 'some' to 'extensive' knowledge after training; validates coverage of feedback practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge of what makes someone a novice or expert
rubrics_metrics.description: Trainees rate their knowledge of distinctions between novice and expert learners on the three-point scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantial increases in 'extensive knowledge' after training signal effective instruction on learner development concepts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge of how human memory works
rubrics_metrics.description: Trainees rate knowledge of human memory on the three-point scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-training increases in 'extensive' knowledge are used to judge coverage of cognitive psychology fundamentals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge of cognitive load
rubrics_metrics.description: Trainees rate knowledge of cognitive load on the three-point scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre/post changes (increase in 'some' and 'extensive') assess whether training effectively communicates cognitive load principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge of what The Carpentries is and what it does
rubrics_metrics.description: Trainees rate their knowledge of The Carpentries and its mission using the three-point scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to evaluate how well training orients trainees to the organization and community roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge of strategies to motivate learners
rubrics_metrics.description: Trainees rate their knowledge of learner motivation strategies on the three-point scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High increases (e.g., up to 87% reporting increased motivation to learn more) indicate effective coverage of motivation strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change in motivation to learn more (by topic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Trainees report whether their motivation to learn more about listed topics (formative vs summative, feedback, novice/expert, memory, cognitive load, Carpentries, motivation strategies) increased after training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as an outcome metric distinct from knowledge/skills; average increase reported ~75% across topics; topic-level variation informs follow-up supports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perception: amount of information reasonable for time allotted
rubrics_metrics.description: Trainees indicate agreement (5-point Likert) with the statement 'The amount of information covered was reasonable for the allotted time.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 86% agreed or strongly agreed, but relatively fewer strongly agreed compared to other items—signals potential overload and a curriculum pacing issue to address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perception: overall atmosphere was welcoming
rubrics_metrics.description: Trainees indicate agreement with 'The overall atmosphere was welcoming' on a 5-point Likert scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High positive response (98% agreed/strongly agreed) used as evidence of inclusive/positive learning environment created by Trainers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perception: material matched event description
rubrics_metrics.description: Trainees indicate agreement with 'The material presented matched the description of the training event' on a 5-point Likert scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High agreement (94%) indicates accurate marketing/communication and alignment between expectations and delivery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perception: training was worth my time
rubrics_metrics.description: Trainees indicate agreement with 'This training was worth my time' on a 5-point Likert scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High positive response (92% agreed/strongly agreed) used as a measure of overall perceived value of the training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Likelihood to recommend (recommendation score)
rubrics_metrics.description: Trainees rate how likely they are to recommend Instructor Training to a friend or colleague on a scale from 1 to 10; five-year averages between 8.43 and 9.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a net-recommendation/advocacy indicator; strong word-of-mouth (81% report hearing about training via word-of-mouth) amplifies importance of this metric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perception of pace
rubrics_metrics.description: Trainees indicate whether the pace was 'too fast', 'too slow', or 'just right'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Majority (56%) report 'just right', but substantial minorities report slightly fast or slow; acknowledges inevitable variation and suggests aiming for the majority's needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perception of balance between lecture and hands-on activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Trainees indicate whether the balance was appropriate (options include 'good', 'too much lecture', 'too much hands-on').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 69% rated balance as good; if off, trainees more often say 'too much lecture' (24%) than 'too much hands-on' (7%), guiding instructional adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructor Trainer performance (clear answers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Trainees rate whether Instructor Trainer(s) gave clear answers to questions (frequency: All of the time/Often/etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High positive ratings (97% all of the time/often) serve as evidence of trainer effectiveness in Q&A and responsiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructor Trainer performance (communication)
rubrics_metrics.description: Trainees rate whether Instructor Trainer(s) were good communicators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High positive ratings (97% all of the time/often) used to validate trainer communication skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructor Trainer performance (considerate)
rubrics_metrics.description: Trainees rate whether Instructor Trainer(s) were considerate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Very high positive ratings (99% all of the time/often) indicate an inclusive, respectful trainer approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructor Trainer performance (enthusiasm)
rubrics_metrics.description: Trainees rate whether Instructor Trainer(s) were enthusiastic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High positive ratings (98% all of the time/often) reinforce trainer engagement as a program strength.

rubrics_metrics.name: Checkout steps (requirements to certify)
rubrics_metrics.description: Three-step checkout required for certification: 1) Homework: contribute to Carpentries lessons or glossary; 2) Discussion: attend an online community discussion; 3) Demo: teach a short demonstration lesson.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understanding of the checkout process is measured at post-workshop; completion of all three steps awards the Carpentries Instructor badge and certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Checkout completion rates and bottlenecks
rubrics_metrics.description: Metrics: percent completing all three steps (around 50-60% historically; 57% completed all three in 2019-2020), percent completing no steps (28%), percent completing some steps (15%). Of non-completers, 85% attended a community discussion, while only 29% completed teaching demo and 23% completed lesson contribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These distributions identify bottlenecks (demo and lesson contribution) and inform targeted interventions to increase certification rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time from training to certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Median time from finishing training to completing certification (2020 median = 78 days).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a process-efficiency metric and to track changes over time; helps set expectations and identify delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time from training to first teaching
rubrics_metrics.description: Median time from completing Instructor Training to teaching first workshop (varied by year; e.g., 182 days in 2020, previously as low as 82 days in 2017).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates how quickly new instructors become active; can be used to infer readiness and local community support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructor teaching activity distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts of how many workshops instructors have taught: most have taught 1 workshop, many 2-5, and over 300 have taught 6+.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to assess retention and ongoing engagement of certified instructors; separate analysis excludes certified instructors who never taught.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification rate (historical and yearly changes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall certification rate since 2013 (51.3%) with year-to-year variation (e.g., 44% in 2014, 57% in 2015, 54% in 2019, 55% in 2020).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitors long-term trends; decreases/increases prompt investigation into causes (e.g., pandemic effects).

rubrics_metrics.name: Number trained, number of trainings, number of certified instructors and trainers
rubrics_metrics.description: Program growth metrics: trainees trained per year (e.g., 1,168 in 2019, 895 in 2020), number of Instructor Trainings per year (e.g., 67 in 2019, 49 in 2020), total certified Instructors (3,335 as of Aug 2021), number of certified Trainers (98 as of Aug 2021).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary metrics to reflect growth and capacity; 'Instructors trained' can be more informative than trainings run because trainings vary in attendance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pipelines for trainees: membership vs open application
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts of trainees trained via organisational Membership agreements versus Open Application scholarships (e.g., 716 via Membership and 178 via Open Application in 2020).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to understand recruitment channels and equity/access; changes in these pipelines may warrant different supports or recruitment strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trainee demographics: country/location
rubrics_metrics.description: Trainees report country of training (limitation: unclear for online trainees); top countries include US, UK, Canada, Australia; map of all countries represented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Geographic distribution informs outreach, time-zone scheduling, and diversity of reach; survey question wording for online trainees is a noted limitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trainee demographics: professional domain and position
rubrics_metrics.description: Trainees report domain (e.g., Computer Science 19%, Bioinformatics/Genomics 16%, Library Science 12%) and position (graduate students 26%, research staff 24%, faculty 16%, postdocs 13%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps understand the audience composition and tailor training examples and materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trainee demographics: ethnic identity (US only)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethnic identity is collected only for US-based trainees; from 2018–2020 US trainees reported White 66%, Asian 17%, Hispanic/Latino(a) 8%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limited geographic collection is a limitation for equity analysis; report recommends deeper exploration of demographics to focus on equity, inclusion, and accessibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: How trainees found out about Instructor Training
rubrics_metrics.description: Trainees indicate source (friend/colleague 55%, advisor/supervisor 26%, Carpentries communications/social media smaller).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Informs marketing/recruitment strategy; high word-of-mouth emphasizes importance of recommendation metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Survey instruments and response scales
rubrics_metrics.description: Skills rated on five-point Likert scales from 'Extremely able' to 'Not at all able'; perceptions on 5-point agreement scales; knowledge on a three-point scale from 'Extensive' to 'Little or no knowledge'; recommendation on a 1-10 scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit measurement scales enable pre/post comparisons and aggregation; consistency in instrument design is important for longitudinal tracking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment limitations to document
rubrics_metrics.description: Noted limitations include unclear country reporting for online trainees, collection of ethnic identity only for US trainees, and not measuring trainees' intentions to certify at time of post-survey.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report recommends re-examining assessment efforts, collecting more consistent demographic data, and measuring intent to checkout to better interpret conversion rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interventions to increase checkout/completion
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed actions to increase certification: clarify instructions/expectations for checkout steps, provide additional support to trainees through the steps, consider whether changes to formats are needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Targeted at the identified bottlenecks (teaching demonstration and lesson contribution); some updates to curriculum instructions have been proposed and Instructor Training Team will work with stakeholders to implement further changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program monitoring and next-step analytics priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Areas for continued assessment: deeper demographic analyses for equity/inclusion/accessibility, analysis of trainee outcomes by path to training (membership vs sponsored), comprehensive understanding of Instructor/Trainer teaching activity and retention, impact of curriculum/policy changes on survey responses, and long-term assessment of Instructors as they begin to teach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These priorities set the agenda for iterative improvement of assessment methods and programmatic decisions.
